items.prompt: Compare typing on a computer to writing with a pencil. Name ONE advantage of each.
items.answer: Typing advantage: you can fix mistakes easily by pressing backspace. Pencil advantage: you can write anywhere without needing electricity.

steps: Computer: easy to fix mistakes, share electronically.
Pencil: works without power, good for drawing too.

items.prompt: A student types her book report and wants to share it with her whole class. She could print 20 copies OR she could email it to her teacher to post online. What is one advantage of posting it online?
items.answer: One advantage of posting it online is that all students can read it on their own devices without using paper or ink.

steps: Posting online: saves paper, no printing needed, everyone can access at the same time from anywhere.

items.prompt: Which would you choose and why: typing your story on a computer OR writing it by hand? Give one reason for your choice.
items.answer: I would choose typing on a computer because I can fix mistakes easily and then email it to my teacher without carrying a paper back and forth.

steps: Pick one option.
Give a specific reason connected to a feature of that tool.

items.prompt: What does it mean to 'collaborate' on writing using a digital tool? Give an example.
items.answer: Collaborating means working together on the same piece of writing. For example, two students could take turns typing sentences in a shared document on a tablet, and both can see the changes immediately.

steps: Collaborate = work together.
Digital tools allow more than one person to work on the same document, even from different places.

items.prompt: A student made a mistake three words back while typing. She does not want to delete everything she just typed. What feature of the keyboard can help her?
items.answer: She can press the backspace key multiple times to delete only the letters back to the mistake. She does not need to delete everything, just the words typed after the error.

steps: Each backspace press removes one character.
She can press it as many times as needed to reach the mistake.

items.prompt: List two types of digital writing tools and describe what you can do with each.
items.answer: 1. Computer: you can type stories, reports, and letters, save them, and email them to others. 2. Tablet: you can type or use a stylus to write on the screen, and you can share work through apps or email.

steps: Name the tool.
Describe at least one writing task you can do with it.

items.prompt: Why might a school want students to learn to type, even if they can write by hand?
items.answer: Learning to type is important because most adults use computers for work, communication, and school. Typing lets you share writing instantly and work on documents with others. It is a skill students will need as they grow older.

steps: Think about how computers are used in everyday life.
Typing is a practical skill for school and careers.

items.prompt: How is sharing a story digitally DIFFERENT from reading your story aloud to the class?
items.answer: Sharing digitally means others can read the story on a screen whenever they want. Reading aloud is a one-time event where listeners must be present. Digital sharing lets many more people access the story at any time.

steps: Reading aloud: one time, everyone must be present, no record unless recorded.
Digital sharing: available anytime, can be read by anyone with the link or file.

items.prompt: Your class wrote a shared story. Your teacher wants to post it on the class website. What steps would you need to take to publish the story digitally?
items.answer: Steps: 1. Type the shared story on a computer. 2. Proofread and make sure it is correct. 3. Save the file. 4. The teacher uploads it to the class website. 5. Families and classmates can now read it online.

steps: Type the story, proofread, save, upload. Each step is part of the digital publishing process.

items.prompt: Describe a time when writing by hand would be BETTER than using a computer.
items.answer: Writing by hand would be better when there is no electricity, no computer available, or when you want to make a personal greeting card or note that feels more special and unique than a typed message.

steps: No power = paper wins.
Personal, handmade writing (cards, notes) often feels more heartfelt.

items.prompt: What does the SHIFT key do on a keyboard?
items.answer: The shift key allows you to type capital letters. When you hold Shift and press a letter, the letter comes out as a capital. Shift is also used to type symbols on the number keys.

steps: Hold Shift + letter = capital letter.
Hold Shift + number key = symbol (!, @, #, etc.).

items.prompt: A student wants to write a book with her best friend who lives in another town. How could digital tools help them write together?
items.answer: They could use a shared document in the cloud (like Google Docs) where both students can type and see each other's changes in real time. They could also email sections back and forth to add to the story.

steps: Digital tools allow collaboration across distances.
Shared documents let two writers work simultaneously.

items.prompt: What does 'publish' mean in the writing process? Where does publishing fall in the writing process (beginning, middle, or end)?
items.answer: Publishing means sharing a final, polished piece of writing with an audience. It comes at the end of the writing process, after drafting, revising, and editing.

steps: The writing process: drafting, revising, editing, then publishing.
Publishing is the last step when the piece is ready for readers.

items.prompt: What should a student do BEFORE publishing a digital story to make sure it is ready?
items.answer: Before publishing, the student should reread the story, check for spelling mistakes, fix any unclear sentences, and make sure the writing is focused on the topic. This is called proofreading or editing.

steps: Proofreading: check spelling, capitalization, punctuation.
Revising: check for clarity, details, and focus.
Both steps come before publishing.

items.prompt: Give one reason why a class newsletter that is published digitally is better than one printed on paper. Give one reason why the printed version might be better.
items.answer: Digital is better because: it can be sent to all families instantly by email and updated if there is a mistake. Print is better because: families who do not have a computer can still read it, and it can be pinned up on the refrigerator.

steps: Digital: speed, easy to update, no printing cost.
Print: accessible to families without devices, physical keepsake.
